calls.head: The Predators will hunt a mismatch
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending Marchessault’s line (Schaefer, Kerfoot and Marchessault) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Penguins’ fourth line is Dewar, Lizotte and Brazeau.

story.head: Marchessault sparks a Predators comeback
paras: Samuel Girard got the scoring started for the Penguins early in the first. Justus Annunen filled in for Juuse Saros for 2:07 in the first before Nashville went back to Saros. Andrei Kuzmenko scored his first goal for Pittsburgh late in the first to make it 2-0 for the Penguins. Jonathan Marchessault got the Predators on the board just over a minute later. Filip Forsberg and Reid Schaefer scored just under four minutes apart early in the second to turn a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 lead. Hendrix Lapierre tied it 3-3 for Pittsburgh midway through the period, but that was the last goal the Penguins would get. Jayden Struble put the Predators ahead for good early in the third.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Saros made 21 saves for the Predators, and Sergei Murashov stopped 25 of 29 at the other end. The Preds moved to 12-6-5, fourth in the Central, while the Penguins dropped to 7-13-2, still last in the Metropolitan.
